How to make your own South Park character.

A few thoughtful choices are enough to create a recognizable avatar. Start simple, then adjust the details that make it yours.

01
Choose your starting point

Open the free studio and select a preset close to your idea. Hair and outfit colors can be changed later. For an imagined scene, switch to the AI generator and describe your character.

02
Give the details a purpose

Adjust hair, hats, clothes, and facial expressions one group at a time. Check the live preview as you go, and use Undo to return to an earlier version.

03
Download a version you love

Choose a background and export a 1024 × 1024 PNG or an SVG. Download the file before leaving. Browser saves keep an editable design on this device and do not sync across browsers.

A little more character in every detail.

Create an original avatar with the South Park paper-cut look: round heads, flat shapes, and expressive faces. Choose recognizable details to suggest a personality. No drawing experience is needed.

A familiar style. An original you.
Start with a recognizable silhouette

Try short hair, curls, long hair, a bob, or spikes, then add a beanie or cap. For a cartoon version of yourself, start with your most recognizable feature. For an invented character, let the silhouette suggest a personality.

Use color to connect the look

Choose an outfit color first, then coordinate the hair and accessories. Compare a bright jacket against snow with a softer outfit in the park. The live preview helps you judge the whole palette.

Let the expression tell the story

A happy, calm, surprised, or grumpy face changes the character's personality. Try glasses or freckles for extra detail, and check that the face remains clear at avatar size.

Keep the scene in balance

Choose snowy mountains, a park, or plain paper to support the character. Use a transparent background when placing the avatar into another design. You can change the scene before exporting another version.

Your avatar, outside the studio.

Choose a destination for your avatar, then match its expression, colors, and background to that use.

Profile pictures

Use a simple background and a clear face for chat apps, community profiles, or a personal account. Preview the image at a small size before settling on tiny details.

Friends and inside jokes

Make a character inspired by a shared hobby, a favorite jacket, or a familiar expression. Use photos or likenesses only with permission, and keep the result considerate of the people involved.

Original character ideas

Use your character as a visual reference for a fictional personality. Save variations to compare different outfits or moods.

Stickers and small projects

A transparent export makes it easier to place your character on a card, a personal sticker layout, or a presentation. Check the requirements of the app or printer you use.

PNG
SVG
The right file for the next idea.

Export the character in your preview as a ready-to-use PNG or a scalable SVG.

PNG, ready to share

The builder exports a 1024 × 1024 PNG. Select Transparent in the scene controls for a file without a background. Some profile-picture apps crop images into a circle, so leave room around the character when checking the result.

SVG, room to grow

SVG preserves vector shapes for resizing in a layout. Check that your destination supports SVG; some apps accept only raster images. Keep the original download for later edits.
